question: In the presence of a 65-year-old patient with no history of interest who comes to the urgency of a hospital, with fever of 39 ° C, meningeal syndrome and signs of severity (coma, BP 80/60 mmHg, poorly perfused), which of the following actions Do you consider more correct at this time?

options.opa: Extract blood cultures, perfuse saline and administer treatment with intravenous dexamethasone, ceftriaxone, vancomycin and ampicillin and then perform cranial CT and lumbar puncture if there is no contraindication and reevaluate treatment after CT.
options.opb: CT scan with as much urgency as possible, eye fundus, subsequent CSF culture and antibiotic treatment directed according to the LCR GRAM data.
options.opc: Put IV antipyretic, start treatment with iv dopamine at alpha dose and when hemodynamically stable, do cranial CT, lumbar puncture and initiate guided antibiotic treatment according to the CSF analytical data.
options.opd: Start treatment with intravenous ceftazidime + acyclovir + vancomycin.
